An ETF (exchange-traded fund) is a basket of many investments, like hundreds of company shares, that you buy as one thing. It trades on the stock exchange just like a single share.

Why people like them:
• *Spread out*: one purchase spreads your money across lots of companies, so a single company doing badly hurts less
• *Low cost*: most ETFs just follow an index (like the world's biggest companies), so their fees are usually low
• *Easy to buy and sell*: you can do it any day the exchange is open

The catch: an ETF's value goes up and down with the market, so you can lose money, especially over short periods.

*ASP* is Finland's state-backed savings scheme for buying your *first home*. A new law has been in force since 1 June 2026.

• *Who can start:* anyone aged 15 or over who has never owned a home. There's no upper age limit anymore.
• *How it works:* you save 50–1 500 € a month for at least 20 months, until you have at least 10% of the home's price.
• *What you get:* the bank pays you 2–4% bonus interest on top. The state also pays part of your ASP loan's interest for the first 10 years, and your loan can get a free state guarantee.
